title: Real Housewife of Cheshire star forced to give away 'evil' dolls
excerpt: Deborah Davies built up a collection of 80 dolls over the last six years after receiving her first one from a follower in 2020
content:
Real Housewife of Cheshire star gives away 'evil' haunted dolls after things 'escalated'

Deborah Davies built up a collection of 80 dolls over the last six years after receiving her first one from a follower in 2020

15:59, 11 Nov 2026

Real Housewife of Cheshire star gives away haunted dolls

A spooked Real Housewives of Cheshire star was forced to give away her 'evil' cache of haunted dolls - after dreaming they were going to kill her.

‌

Celebrity psychic Deborah Davies built up a collection of 80 dolls over the last six years after receiving her first one from a follower in 2020. The 59-year-old cancer survivor said most of her collection was given to her by followers who had experienced poltergeist or haunted activity while owning them.

‌

Debbie's collection featured Annabelle, who hit the headlines in March 2024 after terrifying customers at a charity shop in Edinburgh, Scotland. As she prepared to take the creepy collection out of storage for a Halloween event being held in Knutsford, Cheshire, she claims things escalated.

‌

The mum-of-three said she dreamt she was going to die and heard a male voice tell her, 'Cuddle me and fall asleep'. When her daughter called her to say she had also had a nightmare that her mum was going to die and saw Annabelle in her dream, Deborah knew she needed to get rid of the dolls.

Deborah contacted pal Lee Steer, who owns The Haunted Objects Museum in Rotherham in South Yorkshire, on Facebook begging him to take the 'evil' dolls or she would bury them. The gran-of-nine, who was diagnosed with tonsil cancer in November 2025 but is now cancer-free, admitted she didn't want to take any risks after her 'death dream' and was happy to see them go.

‌

Deborah, from Wilmslow, Cheshire, said: "The first doll was sent to me in 2020. She described poltergeist activity in her home and things were moving and this only started when she bought the item - 95 per cent of the dolls I have in my collection are from people all over the world that were experiencing serious activity.

"Annabelle was from a cancer charity shop up in Edinburgh. People started contacting the shop saying that they were having awful nightmares after passing the doll in the shop. I was going to have some of the dolls in the barn (for my Halloween event). I went to sleep that night and I woke up in the morning and I had dreamt that I had died.

‌

"I heard a male voice say, 'cuddle me and fall asleep', and I knew this meant cuddle me and fall asleep as in 'die'. My daughter rang that morning too and said she'd had a dream that I died too. In the dream she said the main doll Annabelle said, 'It thinks that you're (the doll's) mother'.

"The dolls were in storage at this point. After this, I contacted Lee. I said take my dolls or I'm going to bury them. I'm never normally scared but I've gone through having cancer. Once you've gone through having cancer and then you have a dream that you're going to die, I just didn't want to take any chances."

‌

Worried Deborah claims her doll collection could be 'dangerous' and if Lee or any of his team fall ill, she will gladly take them back and bury them.

‌

Deborah said: "I didn't feel sad at all when Lee took them, I know they needed to go. I told him though there is a lot wrong with these items and he needs to be careful. I said if he falls ill or anything like that, I will take the dolls back and bury them."

After driving down to Manchester to pick up the dolls from Deborah, Lee loaded his red Seat Ibiza with the 80 dolls to make the journey back to the museum. But on the 90-minute drive up the motorway, the ghost hunter claims some of his team began to feel sick and experience a tingling sensation around the mouth.

‌

He also claims his girlfriend, 34-year-old Sarah Carter, has been ill for the last few days since moving the dolls into their museum on October 9. Lee said he can't be sure why everyone started to feel unwell but claims the 'haunted' dolls might have something to do with it. The 40-year-old is now curious to see other people's reactions to the dolls when they come and visit his museum.

Lee, from Rotherham, South Yorkshire, said: "Deborah was absolutely desperate to get rid of them and when we took them, I could see the joy in her. While we were driving home, within about five minutes of setting off, John said his teeth were starting to tingle.

"A bit later on he then said he started to feel sick and 30 minutes in he was really struggling. I then started to feel sick. Everyone in the car felt sick and I think it could be something to do with the dolls. When we got back Sarah felt absolutely sick and she's still sick now. It's put her out for a few days.

"I'm never worried about them. It just intrigues me and makes me want to know more about the dolls. I want to see what other people's reactions are when they come and visit the museum."
